title: Simultaneous spreading of embedded closed-subscheme germ equalities
statement: Let $Y$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $y\in Y$, and let $F$ be a finite set. For each $a\in F$ let $Z_a\hookrightarrow Y$ and $H_a\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], with their defining ideal sheaves [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] $\mathcal I_a,\mathcal J_a\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$. Suppose $(\mathcal I_a)_y=(\mathcal J_a)_y$ as ideals in $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ for every $a\in F$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. There exists a single affine open neighbourhood $U$ of $y$ such that $Z_a\times_Y U=H_a\times_Y U$ as closed subschemes of $U$ for every $a\in F$. Moreover for every subset $S\subseteq F$, the pullback of the scheme-theoretic intersection of the $Z_a$ for $a\in S$ equals the intersection of the corresponding $H_a\times_Y U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. On $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, if $H_a\times_Y U$ has ideal $J_a\subseteq B$, this intersection has ideal $\sum_{a\in S}J_a$. For $S=\varnothing$ it is $U$ (ideal zero); if some $H_a\times_Y U$ with $a\in S$ is empty, it is empty (ideal the unit ideal).

source.place: Tag 01Y3, lemma-local-isomorphism, neighbourhood principle; agent finite-generator ideal-equality and intersection version of returned parent steps 7--8.

proof.text: Choose an affine chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $y$ from the Noetherian affine cover in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], every ideal of $R$ is finitely generated. Put $I_a=\mathcal I_a(V)$ and $J_a=\mathcal J_a(V)$. By [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], the restricted closed subschemes have these ideals and their ideal sheaves on $V$ are $\widetilde I_a$ and $\widetilde J_a$. Choose finite generating lists $i_{a,r}$ and $j_{a,t}$ for these ideals, allowing empty lists. The finite family therefore has only finitely many chosen generators in total.

source.place: Tag 01IN, lemma-closed-subspace-scheme (3)--(4); Noetherian affine chart from Properties Tag 01OV, definition-locally-Noetherian; Algebra Tag 00FM, section-Noetherian.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p$ be the prime of $R$ corresponding to $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] the ring germ map is $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] to the two ideal modules. Their maps to the ring stalk send $i/s$ to $i_y/s_y$ and $j/t$ to $j_y/t_y$: this follows directly by applying the inclusion to representative section germs. Thus the hypothesis on embedded ideal stalks says $I_aR_{\mathfrak p}=J_aR_{\mathfrak p}$, rather than merely an abstract module isomorphism. For every $i_{a,r}$, [lem-exc-localization-ideal-membership-clearing] supplies $s_{a,r}\notin\mathfrak p$ with $s_{a,r}i_{a,r}\in J_a$. Applying the same statement with the ideals interchanged supplies $t_{a,t}\notin\mathfrak p$ with $t_{a,t}j_{a,t}\in I_a$.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6)--(7), interpreted by germs; Algebra Tag 00CD, item-localize-ideal, denominator membership as in IsLocalization.algebraMap_mem_map_algebraMap_iff.

proof.text: Let $f$ be the product of all the $s_{a,r}$ and $t_{a,t}$, with empty product $1$. Primality gives $f\notin\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $U=D_V(f)$ is an affine open neighbourhood of $y$, with ring $B=R_f$. Every factor $s$ of $f$ is invertible in $B$: writing $f=sg$, its inverse is $g/f$. Hence $s_{a,r}i_{a,r}\in J_a$ implies $i_{a,r}/1\in J_aB$, and $t_{a,t}j_{a,t}\in I_a$ implies $j_{a,t}/1\in I_aB$. Since the displayed lists generate, these give $I_aB=J_aB$ for every $a$, on this one $U$. No cancellation in $R$, reducedness, or domain assumption was used; cancellation takes place only by units in $R_f$.

source.place: Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine, and Tag 01HV (3); finite-product denominator argument written by the agent.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], the sections on $D(f)$ of $\widetilde I_a$ and $\widetilde J_a$ are $(I_a)_f$ and $(J_a)_f$. Their images in $B$ are exactly the ideals generated by $I_a$ and $J_a$: a fraction $i/f^n$ is $f^{-n}(i/1)$, and a finite sum of such fractions has a common power denominator and numerator in the original ideal. Consequently the restricted ideal sheaves have the equal affine ideals $I_aB=J_aB$ from step 3, and are equal by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Restricting a closed immersion to an open gives its base change by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic] identifies $Z_a\times_Y U$ with $H_a\times_Y U$ over $U$. Equality here is equality of embedded closed subschemes, through that unique isomorphism over the ambient scheme.

source.place: Tag 01HV (4)--(5), localized sections; Tag 01IN (3)--(4), affine ideal description; Tags 01HO/01HP, lemma-closed-immersion and lemma-characterize-closed-subspace.

proof.text: For a finite subset $S\subseteq F$, the scheme-theoretic intersection is the iterated fibre product over $Y$, with empty product $Y$. For any $T\to U$, a map to its pullback to $U$ amounts, by [def-pc-fibre-product], to maps $T\to Z_a$ over $Y$ for every $a\in S$, together with the fixed $T\to U$. Equivalently these are maps $T\to Z_a\times_Y U$ over $U$. This proves that pullback commutes with the intersection, including $S=\varnothing$, by uniqueness of an object with this universal property. Composing each factor map with the isomorphism from step 4 identifies this functor with that for the $H_a\times_Y U$, proving the asserted equality of intersections over $U$.

source.place: Tag 01JP, definition-fibre-product-schemes: iterated universal property; no separate limit-commutation theorem is used.

proof.text: Write $J_a\subseteq B$ for the ideal of $H_a\times_Y U$ and put $L=\sum_{a\in S}J_a$. The affine closed-subscheme description [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies these factors with $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J_a)$. For an arbitrary test scheme $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] identifies maps $T\to\operatorname{Spec}(B/L)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with the fixed ring map $B\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ annihilating $L$. A ring map annihilates $L$ exactly when it annihilates every $J_a$: each element of $L$ is a finite sum of elements of the $J_a$. By the same morphism correspondence this is exactly a compatible family of maps to all $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J_a)$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}(B/L)$ realizes the intersection universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] and its defining ideal is $L$. For $S=\varnothing$, $L=0$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(B/L)=U$. If one factor is empty, its ideal is $B$: its quotient ring is the ring of sections of the empty scheme, the zero ring. Then $L=B$ and the intersection is $\operatorname{Spec}0=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 01I1, lemma-morphism-into-affine; Tag 01QO, affine description of closed immersions; elementary quotient universal property gives the sum-ideal formula (also Morphisms Tag 0C4H, definition-scheme-theoretic-intersection-union).
